properties.digitization_method: REFIT 2026-09-13 with src/block_fit.py, on top of three prior corrections. (1) The original fix was anchored on a wrong Building 12 position (status.csv had it joined to blklot 4045017, an unrelated residential condo building over 500m away) -- corrected to the real Building 12 (1070 Maryland St, blklot 4114010); see status.csv. (2) The next version placed this box WEST of Building 12 (misreading the Port deck's "away from waterfront buffer zone" as "inland") -- the user corrected this directly: Elevation Sky Park is EAST of Building 12, between it and the water, confirmed against satellite imagery. (3) That east-side box was a hand-computed rectangle, and a user screenshot showed it still crossing a real street (22nd St) -- the hand-computed setback was not reliable. Replaced hand computation with a repeatable tool: src/fetch_streets.py fetches real OSM street centerlines for the whole project area once (cached to data/raw/streets.geojson), and src/block_fit.py polygonizes them (plus the Port jurisdiction boundary) into real block polygons, then fits a box of the requested size inside the correct one, checked programmatically against every nearby street. This box occupies the northern/larger part of the real block bounded by Maryland St (west) and 21st/22nd St (Building 21 takes the southern part, nearer Building 12); block_fit.py fit it at 84% of the requested 406ft x 406ft (165,000 sqft) size -- ~341ft x 341ft -- since the full size didn't clear 21st St from this position. ROTATED 2026-09-13: block_fit.py's earlier version always produced a true-north-aligned box, which looked visibly wrong once rendered -- this area's real street grid (Maryland/Louisiana/Delaware St etc.) is rotated relative to true north, and an axis-aligned box in a rotated block wastes space and doesn't match its neighbors' orientation. fit_box now rotates the box to match the bearing of the nearest real street segment before fitting/shrinking it. properties.why_no_real_parcel: No DataSF Assessor parcel distinct from Building 12 itself was found immediately east of it toward the shoreline -- the area appears to be un-subdivided/not-yet-platted open space or shoreline promenade land (consistent with the D4D's "Slipways Commons" waterfront open-space concept for this part of the site), so there is no candidate blklot to check at all, unlike Noonan/Building 21 where specific (rejected) candidates existed.
properties.regulatory_context: Elevation Sky Park (Elevation XR, in partnership with Brookfield Properties) is a planned interim entertainment venue: three geodesic projection domes and a pyramid under a five-year lease (SF Chronicle, 2025-06-10: "has signed a five-year lease to put four structures (the three domes and a pyramid) on a site between the bay and a historic building"; "on the three-acre site"). Size: the Port's June 25, 2025 community engagement deck labels the venue "Elevation Sky Park (165K sq. ft. / 200+ parking spaces)", so the 165,000 sq ft figure includes parking and is a planned figure; the Chronicle's three-acre site is about 131,000 sq ft, and the two figures do not match. Permits: the same deck says the venue "Will be fully permitted through the Port of San Francisco" (future tense, June 2025); no source read shows that permits were issued. Capacities differ by source: the Chronicle (2026-07-23) gives 200 to 1,250 guests for the domes, the Business Wire release (2026-07-23) 150 to 750. Timing: the deck gave a "TARGET OPENING DATE: Q1 2026" and the Port Commission minutes of 2025-07-08 (p.7) said the venue was "scheduled to open early 2026" (expected dates, both now past). The Chronicle (2026-07-23) reported the domes delayed and "still in the process of being built", with a new manufacturer in Oregon after tariffs and the war in Iran made the original build in Europe too costly. The Business Wire release of 2026-07-23 announced that a one-day festival, Pier Play San Francisco, on Saturday, September 19 "marks the public opening of Elevation Sky Park San Francisco" and that the venue "opens in phases beginning September 2026" (an announcement written before the event). The festival was held on September 19, 2026, but the venue's own page, read 2026-10-12, calls the site "the future home of Elevation Sky Park" and invites sign-ups for "opening announcements", so no source read shows the venue itself open. Status is recorded as planned: no source read describes on-site construction of the domes.
